The Shiu family returned home this afternoon to collect family photos, ancestral coins, calligraphy and paintings, and some clothing. However, due to time constraints and the fact that the unit had been disconnected from water and electricity, they were unable to sort through all their belongings, and plan to return next week to continue packing. In the past, the Shiu family had installed CCTV outside their home; after the land resumption operation, when they returned home, they found that the CCTV had been covered with plastic bags.

The Lands Department recently replied twice, stating that it was only when the Department arranged to hand over the structures to the Civil Engineering and Development Department at the beginning of this year that Mr. Shiu suddenly moved into the squatter hut. They also noted that he is a public housing tenant and does not meet the criteria for rehousing. The Department emphasized that it, together with a social work team, has been in contact with Mr. Shiu since the beginning of the year.

The Shiu family earlier told "集誌社" (Collective Media) that after their father-in-law passed away in 2019, their husband and other siblings jointly inherited the land title through estate administration, and signed off on the land compensation two years ago, but they have yet to receive any compensation payment. The Shiu family continued to refute the claim today, stating that during a fire at Cha Kwo Ling Village in 2016, their husband was already on the scene, escaping with his mother and five pets, and that the incident was even covered and filmed by the media. They expressed dissatisfaction with the Lands Department's claim that their husband was someone who moved in midway.

Another accusation from the Shiu family is that they have not received any compensation since signing the land compensation documents. The Lands Department earlier confirmed that part of the land in question is government land, while the other part is private land. The former owner of the private portion has accepted the government's land compensation offer, but the relevant documents are still pending signing by the former owner's representative lawyer. The Lands Department stated that upon receipt of the signed documents, the land compensation will be disbursed as soon as possible.
